title: Almond horchata
summary: A cold, creamy, cinnamon-scented drink made by blending soaked almonds with water and straining, in the spirit of horchata.
steps: Put the almonds in a bowl with 2 cups of the water and the cinnamon. Cover and soak in the fridge overnight, or at least 8 hours.
Tip the almonds and soaking water into a blender, add the remaining water, the erythritol, vanilla and salt, and blend on high for 2 minutes, until very smooth.
Strain through a nut-milk bag or a sieve lined with a double layer of muslin, squeezing out as much liquid as you can.
Taste for sweetness, then chill. Stir and serve over ice with a dusting of cinnamon.
tips: Most of the almond solids stay in the bag, so the drink carries far fewer carbs than the whole nuts would; the figure shown counts the whole almonds and so overstates it.
The leftover almond pulp can be dried in a low oven and used like almond meal.

origin.history: This is an almond version, not a traditional horchata. The classic Spanish horchata de chufa comes from Valencia and is made from tiger nuts, the small tubers of a sedge grown there since Moorish times; Mexican horchata is made from rice, usually with cinnamon. The name is generally traced to the Latin for barley, an older base for such drinks. Almonds give a similar milky, nutty drink without the starch.
